rv.q: Music Theater Works's SPELLING BEE feels as fresh as ever, perhaps because it invites us to be our sweet, awkward, imaginative childhood selves all over again.
This production is sincere and sure.

I highly recommend this Music Theater Works production of The 25th Annual Putnam County Spelling Bee staged in the lovely and intimate North Stage in the North Shore Center for the Performing Arts for audiences of all ages.
The laughs come easy in this light-hearted romp.
One of the strengths of Music Theater Works’s winning revival is how well it infuses just a touch of rough chaos into an otherwise polished, professional show.
Music Theater Works’ production invites audience members on a punny and prop-filled joyride.
This Music Theater Works performance makes it all so appealing.

Audience members are embarrassed. And there's plenty of time to go out for drinks after the show. The Music Theater Works production of The 25th Annual Putnam County Spelling Bee runs through March 31 at the North Shore Center for the Performing Arts.
Christopher Pazdernik has done Music Theater Works proud, delivering a lovely, funny, and utterly entertaining feel-good show that audiences of all ages will love.
Spelling Bee is an entertaining and effective show with memorable music, lyrics and characters that allow you to be a kid again, where imagination runs free and your care free, inner child comes out.
All of the contestants were strong which makes this a worthwhile theatrical experience.

cn.t: Critics enthusiastically spell out their praise for this "fun," "hilarious," and "delightful" musical, applauding Christopher Pazdernik's fresh direction, the talented cast's energetic performances, and the show's winning blend of heart and humor.
